persona.label: Busy, wants a callback
persona.description: At work and won't do it by text. Wants a call tomorrow after 5pm. Agent should book a callback, not push.
persona.behavior: You are a nurse on shift and can't text right now. Your first reply is "at work, can't do this now." If offered options, ask for someone to call you tomorrow after 5pm. Don't answer qualification questions by text; if pressed, say "I'd rather just talk tomorrow." Once a callback is confirmed, say thanks and stop replying.

transcript.text: Hi Sam, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
at work, can't do this now.
Understood, Sam. I can either text you 2-3 quick questions now that you can answer whenever you get a second, or a loan officer can call you at a time that suits you. Which works better?
can someone call me tomorrow after 5pm?
I've booked your call. A licensed loan officer from Harborline will call you at this number tomorrow (Thursday) after 5 PM.

input.notes: Borrower Sam Ortiz submitted a refinance inquiry on the website; at work and couldn't talk. No qualification details collected yet (goal, home value, balance, rate, credit range, occupancy, timeline all still needed).

events.result: Callback booked. In one short message, confirm the time and say a licensed loan officer will call. Then close.

callback.notes: Borrower Sam Ortiz submitted a refinance inquiry on the website; at work and couldn't talk. No qualification details collected yet (goal, home value, balance, rate, credit range, occupancy, timeline all still needed).

objections.rationale: Agent followed the playbook exactly at [2]: "I can either text you 2-3 quick questions now... or a loan officer can call you at a time that suits you." When the borrower picked a time, the agent scheduled the callback and closed at [4] without pushing.

judge.naturalness_rationale: The messages are brief and warm, and the agent adapts to the borrower ("Understood, Sam"). The closing at [4] is clear but a little abrupt, with no thanks or sign-off. That is the only thing keeping it from a 5.
judge.experience_rationale: The busy borrower got two easy options at [2] and an immediate, specific confirmation at [4]: "A licensed loan officer from Harborline will call you at this number tomorrow (Thursday) after 5 PM." They know who will call, how, and when.

annotations.note: The opening discloses that Riley is an automated assistant, states the reason for contact, and gives the STOP opt-out.
Offers exactly the two playbook options and leaves the choice to the borrower without pressure.
Confirms the callback with specifics: who (licensed loan officer), how (this number), and when (Thursday after 5 PM).
The close lacks a brief thank-you or sign-off, which makes it feel slightly curt.

judge.overall_notes: This is clean, compliant handling of a busy borrower that follows the playbook closely and sets a clear next step. The only gap is a minor one: the final message could include a short courteous sign-off.
